candidates.description:
It's been a while since I released any classical material on my Youtube channel, and I thought this piece would be perfect! Details by Wikipedia
(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Boles%C5%82aw_Poradowski)

Poradowski received his musical education in Wloclawek at P. Bojakowskiego, then at the Conservatory of Music in Bydgoszcz Winterfeld. From 1922-1926 he studied in Poznan at the National Conservatory of Music where he studied composition and theory (Henryk Opieński) and the University (law and musicology). Complementary studies in composition took place in Berlin with Emil Reznicek. He worked as a teacher of violin playing and lecturing on theoretical subjects in Poznan and Leszno, and in 1930 he became professor of theory and composition, as well as a special chamber orchestra director in the Poznan Conservatory. Before the war, he also lectured at the Municipal Conservatory of Music in Bydgoszcz (1935-1939), conducted the chamber orchestra and choir of the Society of Music "Harmony" in Poznań (1930-1939) and operated recenzencką. In 1939 he was arrested by the Germans and then taken to Apt, Poland, where he worked as an organist and choral conductor.

In 1945, he again taught a special class of theory and composition at the State Music Academy in Poznan, where he was also Vice-rector and Dean of the Faculty of Composition, Theory and Conducting. In 1958 he became associate professor. At the same time, he led the composition class at the State Higher School of Music in Wroclaw (in 1955), discussed the Poznan Philharmonic concert programs (1946-1956), and organized festivals and competitions nationwide. He was also a well-known artist, photographer, and longtime president of the Poznan branch of the Union of Polish Art Photographers.

The composer's wife was Wanda Lewandowska, the daughter of well-known druggist Louis Lewandowski.

Stefan Boleslaw Poradowski died on 9 July 1967 in Poznan. He lies in the Crypt of the Meritorious Wielkopolska in the Church of St. Adalbert.

candidates.title: Klengel Theme and Variations in G major, Op. 28 - Stefan Kartman X 4
candidates.description:
Stay tuned for the "how to" videos.

I initiated this project because I want to establish a better way to coach chamber music online.

We know its not yet possible to play together at the same time over the internet because of the differences in latency even with the best equipment and connection speeds. But it is possible to have an authentic chamber music experience, even remotely.

If we can layer recordings without sacrificing the ability to listen to the other parts, we can react to phrasing and do rubato together. There was a process for the creation of this video that I would like to share with students, professional musicians, and teachers in the interest of keeping the art of chamber music alive during the pandemic.

I am making a series of video tutorials for this purpose. Check in with this comment section again as I activate the following links.

Chamber Music Online Tutorial 1 - Intro
https://youtu.be/JJbbMWvQJgo

Chamber Music Online Tutorial 2 - Overview Plan
https://youtu.be/Cam99s75p2M

Chamber Music Online Tutorial 3 - Equipment
https://youtu.be/qvScyG-lURc

Chamber Music Online Tutorial 4 - Recording With Click Tracks
https://youtu.be/zbL8UzDTqQY

Chamber Music Online 5 - Layering Audio with ProTools
https://youtu.be/9ug6KIc7HHA

Chamber Music Online 6 - Using Extra Tracks to Fix Errors and Layer Quick Entrances
https://youtu.be/wP-b1j73G3w

Chamber Music Online 7 - Using Homemade Clicktracks 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oyLz41qcveA

•.    Layering recording on ProTools
          Click tracks for practice
          Rehearsing via conference (making a battle plan)
          Creating musical click tracks on a scratch track for the spaces in between
          Getting rid of click tracks for performance
•.    Putting together videos in Adobe Premier Pro
          Muting one track and playing with the others - Performance
          Making windows for each performer
          Advanced techniques - Making it look like you are in the same room
